title: LOUISVILLE FALL HARVEST FESTIVAL
full_story:
The first event for the 75th Annual Louisville Fall Harvest Festival will be Wednesday night when the Rotary Club and Louisville Community Church’s will have a Trunk or Treat on the square from 6 to 7:30 pm.  The Rotary Club will be grilling Salt & Strings Butchery Bub Chops and Blair’s Slaughtering & Processing, Inc pork burgers and hot dogs.

The Kiddie Parade kicks things off Friday afternoon at 2 pm, with Full Armor Christian School serving treats at the old Soda Fountain and the Red Brush Christian Church will be serving apple cider and the Louisville Christian Church will be serving free water near the pocket park.  From 4 to 6 pm the Methodist Church will be offering free chili with Das-zle Dance and tumble performing at 5:30 pm.  From 5:30 to 6:30 pm will be the past Queen reception at the State Bank Suite.  At 6:15 pm Sylvia and Meila Robey will sing on stage.  The Little Miss, JR Miss, and Queen pageants will be held at 7:00 pm.  There are 6 contestants vying for the title of Louisville Fall Festival Queen, The current Queen is Mila Zink.  There are 7 contestants in the JR Miss contest, the current JR Miss is Elsie Anderson, and there are 10 young ladies vying for the Little Miss title held by Landrey Eade.

The glow 5K Walk, Run will take place after the pageants.  From 9 to 10 pm there will be music on the square with Seth Schnautz.

Saturday starts with the Rotary Pancake breakfast from 7 to Noon, with tickets now on sale.  The FFA, AG Mechanics Tractor show will be on the east side of the square and kids activities will start at 8 am and the Clay County Genealogical Society Library will have an open house.  The Clay County Cruisers Car Show begins at 9, there will also be a greased pig contest, sponsored by the Hoosier Prairie Baptist Church, and a country store will open at the old Clay County Jail with free coffee and popcorn.

The Princess pageant will be on the main stage at 10 am with special guest Briley Mullins performing.  Starting at 11 am will be the Chili Cook Off Contest, hosted by the North Clay FCCLA and the Louisville Chamber of Commerce, with tastings available to 1 pm.  Contestants should bring their chili to the pocket park by 10:45 am.  Sign up by emailing [email protected], the winner will get a $50 prize.  At 11:30 Power and Grace Tumbling will perform on the main stage.  At 1 pm Deputy Trevin Smith and his K9 Chief will have a demonstration.  The parade is at 2 pm, Katrina Van Dyke has been named as the parade marshal.  Following the parade the crowning of the Queens and the Rotary Basket Raffle winners will be announced.

For the Parade floats, cars, tractors, bands and Queens will line up at the grade school, horses will line up at the city park, Louisville Queens and contestants will line up on Magnolia Street, and Emergency Services will line up at the high school.  Handicap parking for the parade will be available on the east side of the square.

All weekend there will be arts, and crafts, food vendors, basket raffle and inflatables for the kids.

In conjunction with the Fall Harvest Festival the Louisville American Legion will have a meat shoot on Sunday, November 1st at 11 am.

title: FLORA HALLOWEEN PARADE
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce Halloween Parade is Saturday night, at 7:00 pm.  There is no theme, so entrants can use their own creativity when planning the entry.  All entries to the parade must be registered with the Chamber in order to participate.  Please register at the chamber no later than Noon on Friday.  The Chamber office is open on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday from 8 am to 5 pm.

The parade route will start at The Depot (State Street) and end at Christ Church (Olive Street).  Emergency vehicles will be allowed to sound their sirens during the parade.

Staging areas will be given the day you register and parade numbers will be given the day of the parade when you check in.  Location of your Staging Area will be based on the type of entry.  The Chamber is asking everyone to please be respectful of the staging areas and leave them in the same condition they were in upon arrival.  All entries must check in with the staging area volunteer in the brightly colored vest, to officially check in and verify the entry has their card number on their entry for judging.  Bands, queens, and political entries do not need parade cards but do need to check in with the stage volunteer.

Horses are to unload at the Price Less IGA at 6 pm with a mandatory police escort to the grass area of GSI beginning at 6:15.  If you miss the police escort you will not be permitted in the parade.

Handicap spectators may park at Southern Lumber Company (corner of E. North Ave & South Mill) and please use the south entrance closest to the tracks.

All entries are required to register.  A $10 late fee will be required by any unregistered participant if they register after Noon on Friday, October 30th.  There will be absolutely no throwing of candy from vehicles or trailers/float, candy can be handed out or tossed if you are a walker on the sides of the street.  If an entry is caught throwing, they will be disqualified from judging.

Performance groups may stop at the judging stand and do a performance no longer than 90 seconds.  Any performance longer than 90 seconds will disqualify you from judging.

title: SANTA SMILES APPLICATIONS
full_story:
Applications for Santa Smiles need to be turned in by Sunday.

Applications can be picked up at the Clay City Village Hall, Xenia Village Hall, Louisville Village Hall, Louisville Banking Company, or Salt & Strings Butchery.  In Flora applications are available at the Flora City Hall, Flora Library, CEFS, and the office of Todd Fender at the Clay County Housing Authority.  The Clay County Health Department will give their applications to their clients.

title: IUKA ACCIDENT
full_story:
A teenager from Highland is lucky to be uninjured after swerving to miss a deer in rural Marion County Friday night.

According to the Marion County Sheriff’s Department, the seventeen-year-old was driving on the Route 161 Extension near the Klomp Road intersection in Iuka just before 10:30 pm.

Deputies say the teen veered off the road to avoid a deer, causing his van to roll over into a roadside ditch.

Paramedics checked out the juvenile at the crash site, but he declined further medical treatment at a hospital.  The Marion County Sherrif, Iuka Fire Department, and United Medical Response crews responded to the scene.

title: UNEMPLOYMENT
full_story:
Clay County’s job market is holding steady, but regional hiring tells a mixed story.

Latest figures from the Illinois Department of Employment Security show Clay County’s unemployment rate held firm at 3.6% in September, matching August’s rate and dropping over a full percentage point from last year.

While the workforce grew by nearly 30 employed residents, the total number of people filing for unemployment claims actually rose by 66, bringing the county’s total jobless count to 268.

Looking across the region, unemployment rates remained mostly locked in place.  Jasper County claims the area’s lowest jobless rate at a steady 2.6%, while Marion County sits at the highest at 4.2%.  Elsewhere, Wayne County saw a slight drop in unemployment, while Effingham and Fayette County held flat.

The Illinois Department of Employment Security reports there are 375 fewer jobs in the Centralia-Mt. Vernon labor market than a year ago.  The biggest employment gains are private education-health services up 375 jobs and government up 175 jobs.

Year-over-year payroll totals were unchanged in construction, information, and other services.

Payroll job losses occurred among employers in the trade-transportation-utilities down 300 jobs, professional-business services down 275 jobs, leisure-hospitality and manufacturing both down 125 jobs, and financial activities were down 100 jobs.

The state unemployment rate was at 4.2% for September down .7%.  The national unemployment rate was 4% down three tenths of a percent.

title: DAYLIGHT SAVING TIME ENDS
full_story:
Millions of Americans will turn back their clocks Saturday night, before going to bed, marking the end of Daylight-Saving Time in 2026.

The controversial practice of “springing forward” and “falling back” has been observed in most states for decades.  Under the current Daylight-Saving Time period, most Americans lose an hour of sleep on the second Sunday of March and gain an hour the first Sunday of November.

Daylight Saving Time ends Sunday, November 1st at 2 am.  We will “fall back,” turning our clocks back to 1 am, gaining an extra hour of sleep.

As the clock turns back an hour on that weekend, it’s also a good time to check your smoke detectors and make sure you have a fire escape plan that allows all family members to get out in two minutes if a fire occurs.

In 2005 Daylight Saving Time was shifted to begin on the second Sunday of March and end on the first Sunday of November.  A Department of Energy study found the extra daylight saves around 0.5% in total electricity daily in the US, equaling energy savings of 1.3 billion kilowatt-hours annually.

Next year, Daylight saving time will begin on Sunday, March 14th.

title: IUKA MAN INJURED
full_story:
An elderly Iuka man is recovering after a frightening lawn mower accident late Thursday afternoon.

Iuka fire Chief Kenny Eagan says firemen were called out around 4 pm to a home on Cash Road north of Iuka.  Upon arrival, emergency crews found Bill Cash with his foot trapped under the deck of a zero-turn riding mower.

Chief Eagan says the mower was still running and the wheels were spinning after the machine had collided with a pole.  Fortunately, the mower’s blades were not engaged.

Cash had been trapped underneath the deck for twenty to thirty minutes before help arrived.  After shutting down the mower, firemen helped Cash to his feet, allowing him to free the trapped foot.

Cash was transported to Salem Township Hospital for the treatment of apparent minor injuries.
